verdicts.reason: Without Samuel in the valley, no one befriends Adam and finally tells him that Cathy is Kate. That chain is what leads to Adam's confrontation with her and the move to Salinas.
The inheritance pays for the Salinas Valley ranch and later funds the lettuce gamble. Losing that money is what drives Cal to try to earn it back.
Her escape under a false identity puts her in Edwards's power. That is what eventually brings her to the Trask door.
The beating is why the broken Cathy turns up helpless on the Trasks' porch.
Without her arrival Adam never meets and marries her.
The marriage takes Adam and the pregnant Cathy to California, where the twins are born.
It only clouds the twins' paternity. The twins are still born, Cathy still leaves, and Cal still reveals her to Aron.
Settling near King City is what brings Adam into Samuel's orbit. It also places Cathy within reach of Salinas.
The friendship begun here is why Samuel later feels bound to tell Adam the truth about Kate.
It deepens Lee's bond with Samuel, but Lee still serves the family and the twins still get named. No later step depends on it.
Cathy waits until after the birth to leave, and without the twins there is no Cal or Aron at all.
Her violent departure is what sends her to Faye's and leaves Adam bound to her memory. Both lead toward the later revelations.
Town gossip about the runaway wife and Samuel's knowledge do not hinge on Quinn's questioning. Cal still learns the truth through Adam.
Without her becoming Kate in a Salinas brothel, there is no madam for Samuel to name or for Cal to show Aron.
Even as one of Faye's women, Kate would still be in a Salinas brothel where Samuel could name her and Cal could take Aron. Owning the house is not what the reveal needs.
It starts Adam's recovery, but the decisive release comes from Samuel's later disclosure. The boys would be named and raised regardless.
The naming and the Cain and Abel talk matter thematically, but nothing later depends on this scene.
Samuel had kept silent for years and speaks only because he is leaving and will not see Adam again.
This disclosure is what sends Adam to confront Kate.
Freed of Cathy, Adam can move to Salinas, and his knowledge is what he later passes on to Cal.
It establishes Abra's preference for Aron, but Cal's reveal is driven by Adam's rejection, not by this rivalry.
Aron's faith in a pure dead mother shapes how hard the blow lands, but Cal takes him to Kate for his own reasons regardless.
Living in Salinas puts the twins in Kate's town and leads to the lettuce venture and Cal's night prowling.
Adam's loss is the whole reason Cal tries to make money to give him.
Aron's piety makes him fragile, but he still goes to Stanford and Adam still prefers him. Cal's reveal follows the rejection either way.
On the way home from the raid Adam tells Cal about his mother, which is how Cal learns who Kate is.
Shadowing her is how Cal confirms her identity and learns where she lives, the knowledge he uses to lead Aron there.
Cal already knows who and where Kate is from following her, so he could still take Aron to her house without this meeting.
The war creates the bean market Cal profits from, and Adam's draft-board guilt is why he rejects the money as war profit.
Cal has no capital to contract the beans without Lee's loan.
The bean profit is the gift Cal offers and Adam refuses.
Aron would be home at Thanksgiving either way, and Adam's preference for him does not depend on Stanford.
Adam's rejection, and his preference for Aron's goodness, provokes Cal's jealous revenge that same night.
This is the focal event.
